newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kukdong recurring profit seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Kukdong recurring profit seen rising.

text.p: South Korea's Kukdong City Gas Co forecast its recurring profit would rise to 16 billion won in calendar 1997, up from 12.6 billion won a year earlier, a company spokesman said on Friday.
"We expect to post 16 billion won in recurring profit on sales of 220 billion won this year," Kim Jang-kyu told Reuters.
The city gas supplier's sales stood at 196.7 billion won last year, up from 171.3 billion in 1995.
But he said the financial failure of Seyang Information and Communication Co in February was expected to damage Kukdong's net account this year.
Kukdong has guaranteed payment of 27 billion won liabilties owed by Seyang. It also holds nine billion won worth of convertible bonds issued by the sister company.
He said Kukdong, whose former chairman was the biggest shareholder in Seyang, would have to redeem much of the debts on behalf of Seyang over the next few years.
But he declined to elaborate on Seyang's failure.
Kukdong announced earlier on Friday the LG Group became its largest shareholder with a 51 percent stake.

LG Electronics Inc bought a 23 percent stake from Kukdong's former chairman Chang Hong-son and three other shareholders. LG Cable and Machinery Ltd and LG-Caltex Oil Corp already hold a combined 28 percent stake.
